Guides / Catching / Catch rules

Catch rules

Every catch rule, its default, the Catch list and "never send" protections.

Catch rules decide what gets a ball, which ball, and what happens to duplicates. The first rule a wild Pokémon matches wins.

RuleDefaultWhat it does
New speciesOnCatch anything not in your Pokédex yet.
New looksOffCatch a species in a look you've never had (normal, or a special look you have no stamp for).
Shiny / Void / PrismaticOnCatch every special look.
Perfect IVsOnCatch any Pokémon with all six IVs at 31 (known before the throw).
LegendariesOnCatch every legendary and Mythical. "Call me first" makes them wait 2 minutes for you.
Catch listEmptyUp to 60 exact species, plus categories (a type, or Alpha / Common / Uncommon / Rare / Legendary), always worth a ball even if you own them. An IV minimum skips weaker ones before a ball is thrown. The family button makes an entry catch its whole evolution line too.
Catch everythingOffEvery wild Pokémon gets a few balls.
BallAutoThrow this special ball while you have any, then the usual order.
Master BallPrismaticWhen to use a Master Ball (see Master Ball).
Auto-restock20 Poké BallsBuy Poké Balls back up to this number after every battle (and Ultra Balls once the Mart sells them).
Auto-sell NuggetsOffNuggets and Big Nuggets turn straight into money.
Auto-sell spare ballsOffPer ball, a number to keep; found balls above it sell at the buy-back price.
Send duplicates to the ProfessorOffKeeps your best of each species + look and sends the rest (see the Professor).
Battle rare finds myselfOnSpecials wait 2 minutes for you to battle them.
Bosses: Call me firstOffA new island boss waits 2 minutes for you to start it.
Never send (species)EmptyUp to 60 species whose every copy stays, extras too (see below).
Auto-evolveOnOff = nothing evolves on its own anywhere; Pokémon wait as "Ready to evolve" until you press Evolve.
Living dexOffYour best copy of each species never evolves on its own, so you keep one of every stage.
Use evolution itemsOffStones and evolution items in your Bag are used by themselves on the Pokémon that can use them.

Evolving

  • Auto-evolve (on by default): Pokémon evolve on their own when they reach their evolution (level-ups, catches, while hidden or closed). Switched off, nothing evolves by itself, not even with the two options below: each one waits with the PC's green arrow (filter: Ready to evolve) until you press Evolve.
  • Living dex (off by default): your best copy of each species (party first, then perfect IVs, Alpha, IVs, level) stays as it is. It gets the green arrow and one log line instead; extra copies evolve as usual. You can still evolve it yourself from the PC.
  • Use evolution items (off by default; it asks first, since it uses the stones already in your Bag): stones and evolution items go straight to the Pokémon that can use them, party first, then the best IVs. Never the Linking Cord, and never specials, Perfect-IV Pokémon, branching lines (Eevee…: your pick), an Everstone holder, the Day Care, fused Pokémon, one on a trade or your Living dex copy.

"Never send" protections

Duplicates you protect are never sent to the Professor automatically. Your party, Day Care, Mega Stone holders, fused Pokémon, unrevealed babies and Pokémon on a trade are always safe.

ProtectDefault
ShinyOn
VoidOn
PrismaticOn
PerfectOn
AlphaOn
LegendaryOn
RareOff
HatchedOff
Holding an itemOn
CostumeOn
SpectralOn
MirageOn
GildedOn
GlitchedOn

Species list: Catch rules → Never send → Species holds up to 60 species (or click the lock on a Pokédex page). Every copy of those stays: auto-send and Send duplicates skip them all. Picking them yourself in the PC and pressing Send still works, after a heads-up.
